newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Beijing instructed Chinese media not to report on seven kinds of news related to the Hong Kong handover on June 30, including unflattering events, differences between the economies and policies in Hong Kong and China's neighbouring Guangdong province, arguments between employers and employees in the territory, the comments and actions of the British government and major social problems on the mainland.

-- A flood of fake 1,000-dollar notes found in Hong Kong has led to suspicions that mainland tourists were hired to pass along the phony bills. Hongkong Bank found 224 fake notes in the first four months of the year, a 120 percent increase over 1996.
-- SING TAO -- A report predicted HK$585 billion in investment would flow into Hong Kong from China this year.
-- WEN WEI PO -- Trade between China and Taiwan recovered in the first quarter of this year, reaching US$5.1 billion, representing a 7.2 percent increase from last year.
-- Post-handover leader Tung Chee-hwa stressed that Hong Kong's economic prosperity should be maintained and expressed support to the new "Free Market Index".
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong may tighten supervision of red-chip companies by demanding explanations of how they will invest money raised through public offerings.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Members of the public were invited to submit their views on arrangements for Hong Kong's first post-handover legislative elections within two weeks.

-- China's most profitable department store operator Wangfujing -- 50 percent owned by red chip Beijing Enterprises -- was to launch a promotion in Hong Kong offering fashion and entertainment companies easier access to China's consumer market.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Beijing Enterprises smashed the territory's record for initial public offerings when it announced its flotation was 1,275 times oversubscribed.
